title: The normalized transition sequence after choosing a residue flat model
statement: For X, A, J, N and n as in lem-sfb-adic-finite-transition-tensor-sequence, fix a K-flat independent-coefficients complex P over the residue coefficient sheaf together with an isomorphism Q(P) to the residue reduction. Then there exist a residue module M and a short exact complex sequence S over A whose last two localized terms identify with the normalized reductions at n+1 and n, whose localized quotient map agrees with adicFiniteTransition, and whose first homology in every degree is the restriction of the ordinary tensor-test homology of P with M[0].

source.place: Tag 09C2, proof of (1), coefficient-kernel tensor sequence after fixing a K-flat residue model

proof.text: Choose a termwise flat K-flat representative K of N. Its residue scalar extension K0 is K-flat and represents the residue reduction. Prove the strict successor g is epic degreewise: the coefficient quotient has a set-theoretic section, constant sheafification carries this to a section on underlying sets, and reductionStep_existsUnique plus restricted tensor extensionality give cancellation. Take S to be the canonical kernel sequence of g, hence short exact.

Use the inverses of the specified strict reduction level comparisons as the two endpoint isomorphisms. The existing normalized strict successor identity gives exactly the localized second-arrow square. No derived transition is replaced or redefined.

Construct M explicitly as the constant sheafification of the actual kernel of A/J^(n+2) -> A/J^(n+1), with its quotient A/J action justified by the proved annihilation lemma. The ordinary flat-tensor kernel identification gives an isomorphism from S.X1 to restriction of M tensored termwise with K.

Apply the proved independent-coefficient tensor cancellation, natural in K, to pass to the residue scalar extension K0. The single-factor total tensor comparison and symmetry identify this termwise tensor with K0 tensor M[0]. Exact restriction commutes with homology. Finally coefficientModelTensorTest_iso transports the result along Q(K0) isomorphic to Q(P), using K-flatness of both representatives.

proof_origin.place: Tag 09C2, proof of (1): explicit coefficient kernel, canonical strict kernel sequence, normalized successor, and residue tensor homology transport. Ordinary flat-tensor identification is isolated from the derived assembly.

from.place: coefficient-kernel construction after choosing the residue model

lean.statement:
theorem adicFiniteTransition_tensor_sequence_core
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (A : Type (max v (u + 1))) [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (N : adicFiniteAmbient.{u, v} X A) (n : ℕ)
    (P : Cx (constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X)
      (adicFiniteCoeff J 0)))
    (_hP : P.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients)
    (_eP : Nonempty ((Q _).obj P ≅ adicFiniteReduction.{u, v} X J N 0)) :
    ∃ (M : Mod (constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X)
        (adicFiniteCoeff J 0)))
      (S : ShortComplex (Cx (constant (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A))),
      S.ShortExact ∧
      ∃ (e₂ : (Q _).obj S.X₂ ≅ adicFiniteUnderlying.{u, v} X J N (n + 1))
        (e₃ : (Q _).obj S.X₃ ≅ adicFiniteUnderlying.{u, v} X J N n),
        (Q _).map S.g ≫ e₃.hom = e₂.hom ≫ adicFiniteTransition.{u, v} X J N n ∧
        ∀ q : ℤ, Nonempty (S.X₁.homology q ≅
          (res (quotient (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A J 0)).obj
            (coefficientModelTensorTest _ P M q))
